name: Peculiar Osadebay-Strömberg
creator: Peculiar Osadebay-Strömberg
description: Working out of a converted cold-storage unit in Tier 2's Garfield Annexe, Osadebay-Strömberg engineers living geneware organisms into slow-motion sculptures that grow, die, and decompose over installation cycles of eighteen to ninety days. Her signature series, Inheritance Fauna, features creatures that visibly express the genetic markers of deceased Shelf residents — commissioned by families who cannot afford memorial services. The work occupies a legal gray zone, since her organisms are technically patented HelixCorp geneware chassis modified without license.
medium: physical installation — living geneware organisms, temperature-controlled vivariums, optional neural-feed documentation feed
cultural_impact: Osadebay-Strömberg has made grief and genetic memory into a public conversation, forcing corponation IP law into conflict with cultural mourning practices; her work is cited in three active Seam Rights litigation cases.
controversy: HelixCorp has issued two cease-and-desist orders for unlicensed chassis modification; the second order was withdrawn after a viral neural-feed campaign framed prosecution as criminalizing bereavement. She continues to operate under deliberate legal ambiguity.
story_hooks: A Shelf family commissions Osadebay-Strömberg to memorialize a relative whose genetic records were expunged by a corponation — she must reconstruct the genome from black-market tissue samples, drawing dangerous attention.

One of her Inheritance Fauna organisms begins exhibiting behaviors inconsistent with its designed parameters, suggesting the geneware chassis retains more of its original HelixCorp programming than anyone knew.
A Tier 4 corporate collector offers an obscene sum to acquire a living piece before it completes its death cycle — the family who commissioned it refuses to sell, and the collector has other means.
